title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 49
paragraphs: Artabanus answered: “O king, no one with sense could fault this army, nor the number of the ships; and indeed, if you assemble more, the two things I am speaking of will become only more hostile. These two things are the land and the sea. Nowhere in the sea, I suppose, is there a harbor large enough to receive this fleet of yours and keep the ships safe if a storm should arise — and it is not one such harbor that is needed, but harbors of that size along the whole of the coastline past which you are sailing. If there are no harbors to receive your ships, know that circumstance will master men, not men circumstance. Having told you of one of the two things, I come now to the other. The land, I say, becomes hostile to you in this way: even if nothing rises up to oppose you, the land becomes more hostile the further you advance, as you steal on still further and further; for men never know satiety of good fortune. And this I tell you: with no one standing against you, the country you traverse, growing larger as time goes on, will produce famine for you. The best condition for a man is this: when taking counsel, to feel fear, and to reckon on suffering everything that might come; but in doing the deed, to be bold.”
